bug_semantics: The reported mechanism is that POST /api/v1/invitation-code/redeem has no DeveloperDep or API-key dependency and treats an eight-character invitation code as the sole credential; a valid, unexpired, unredeemed code is looked up and exchanged for an SDK-scoped access JWT, a refresh token, and the bound user_id. Thus anyone who obtains a still-valid code can redeem it first. This is not actually missing authentication: the code was deliberately designed as a single-use bearer credential for standalone/mobile onboarding, and the CNA ultimately rejected CVE-2026-78154 as a false positive.
flaw_origin: PR #455 intentionally created the public bearer-code onboarding flow. Its first member commit 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a added backend/app/api/routes/v1/user_invitation_code.py with the public redeem handler and backend/app/services/user_invitation_code_service.py with the code lookup and SDK access/refresh-token issuance. The later squash landing d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd, revocation hardening, async-to-sync refactor, schema move, and documentation clarification did not originate the reported mechanism. The alleged flaw is therefore the original, explicit product design rather than a later accidental authentication regression.
ai_marker: absent; git cat-file -p 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a shows author Bartosz Michalak <barmic12@gmail.com>, committer Bartosz Michalak <barmic12@gmail.com>, subject 'feat(backend): add invitation code for SDK user onboarding', and no trailers; neither identity is a bot and there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI marker in the BIC commit object.
evidence: First-party origin: https://github.com/the-momentum/open-wearables/issues/430 specifies a seven-day, single-use code generated by an authenticated developer and a public token-exchange endpoint; https://github.com/the-momentum/open-wearables/pull/455 repeats that public design and its manual redemption test. This establishes intent before the reported advisory.

Smallest BIC and attack path: git show 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a adds backend/app/api/routes/v1/user_invitation_code.py (redeem_invitation_code accepts only payload and DbSession, explicitly says no authentication is required, then calls redeem) and backend/app/services/user_invitation_code_service.py (get_valid_by_code, mark_redeemed, create_sdk_user_token, create_sdk_refresh_token, and return both tokens plus user_id). It also adds the router registration, model, repository, and schema in one 237-line feature commit.

Parent absence: 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a has immediate parent bef70833378058e24f5800ac537721a9aaaeafde. A direct git ls-tree -r --name-only of that parent for the route, service, repository, schema, and model paths returned zero entries; the BIC diff marks all mechanism files as new.

Squash decomposition: GitHub's PR-commit endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/the-momentum/open-wearables/pulls/455/commits exposes the five-member chain 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a -> 0009bad1934ac3d3b7aaa64cda77a6b67941a145 -> 36ac4f6a047e25d8f3edab65bbde4097338624e8 -> 2ddc322a1bb475beaf0dc32161f00c790fc19423 -> 03ed8fb8dbb914bc0b93a52f5374bfe11896cdeb. git rev-parse shows PR head 03ed8fb8dbb914bc0b93a52f5374bfe11896cdeb and squash landing d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd share tree 46cfdbd20837852e75f987c918ecb825f75832a5. The first member already contains the complete reported route-to-token mechanism, so later members and the squash aggregate are not the BIC.

Version boundary: git diff --name-status 0.2.2 0.3 shows the route and service added; git tag --contains d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd includes 0.3, every 0.4/0.5/0.6 release (including the advisory's 0.6.2), 0.6.3, and 0.7.0. Therefore the behavior begins in release 0.3, is present in 0.6.2, and was not removed at a patched boundary after 0.6.2.

No fix: git log --all -- backend/app/api/routes/v1/user_invitation_code.py finds only the squash landing, an async-to-sync refactor, a schema-directory refactor, and documentation-only clarification 78f8e604be6ac63138e4a55a23a972f4d101450c. The clarification remains explicit that redemption is public and returns the tokens; it is contained in 0.7.0, and origin/main at f766b5a0a45b091828317d30c5e516574adfbe61 retains the flow. Hence neither 78f8e604be6ac63138e4a55a23a972f4d101450c nor any later commit is a security fix.

Disposition: report https://github.com/the-momentum/open-wearables/issues/1274 was closed by the maintainer as by-design because the invitation code is the credential, is generated through authenticated issuance, is high-entropy/single-use/expiring, and yields SDK-scoped tokens. The authoritative CVE API record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-78154 is REJECTED as of 2026-08-25 and says further investigation found no security issue for exactly that reason. This also explains why there is no remediation SHA.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file -p 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a shows human author and committer Bartosz Michalak and a trailer-free commit message. No PR-body, branch-name, later review-bot, or fix-side signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability-first trace reaches the public redeem handler and follows payload.code into a one-time valid-code lookup and then SDK access/refresh-token issuance. Historical decomposition matters because main contains a GitHub squash commit: the exact PR head tree equals the squash landing tree, while the first recoverable member commit already adds every causal line and its immediate parent contains none of those files. That member is therefore the smallest real BIC. The landing first appears between tags 0.2.2 and 0.3 and remains in releases beyond the bundle's stated 0.6.2 bound, so there is no patched version boundary or fix commit. First-party design records, the maintainer disposition, and the CNA's rejected record show that possession of the invitation code is intended authentication, making the advisory a false positive rather than an unremediated authentication regression. Independently of that disposition, the only attribution evidence allowed by the protocol—the BIC commit object—has a human author/committer and no AI trailer or bot marker, so the causal attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched by design, not an evidentiary gap: no fix_sha or direct_fix_sha exists because the project retained the public bearer-code flow and VulDB rejected CVE-2026-78154 as a false positive. The advisory's claimed upper bound of 0.6.2 is not a patched boundary; the same behavior is present in 0.6.3, 0.7.0, and the validated origin/main history.
